problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,0,4)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-t \\ y=4+3t \\ z=-6+5t.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨-3,0,4⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-t \\ y=4+3t \\ z=-6+5t\end{aligned}\,⇒\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2,4,-6⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-1,3,5⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

  

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-1,3,5⟩.$ So, a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-1,3,5⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,3,5⟩ & =⟨-3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨-1,3,5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,3,5⟩ & =23.\end{aligned}
$$
